I am a 56-year-old farmer in Quzhou County, and I have farmed this land for over three decades. With my university education, I keep up with the extension station recommendations and soil science reports, but I also know what this particular patch of North China Plain soil does year after year. At my age, I do not gamble on unfamiliar cash crops; the wheat–maize double-cropping system is the backbone of my household income and food security. 

This autumn I will plant **winter wheat** across all 10 mu. I use an improved high-yielding variety such as Jimai 22 or Shixin 828, not traditional seed, because the lodging resistance and grain weight are worth the extra cost. I prepare the seedbed with rotary tillage to break up the wheat–maize stubble interface and create a fine tilth for uniform germination. For fertility, I apply a basal compound fertilizer plus a top-dressing at jointing: about 17 kg N, 7 kg P₂O₅ and 4 kg K₂O per mu in total, which is slightly lower than what some neighbors dump but matches the soil-test results I had done last year. Water is precious, so I irrigate four times—overwintering, green-up, jointing and grain filling—using border irrigation from the village well. I also spray four times: a pre-emergence herbicide, a fungicide at flag-leaf stage, and two insecticide applications for aphids and armyworm. I expect roughly 560 kg/mu if the spring frost cooperates.

Immediately after wheat harvest in early June, I will direct-seed **summer maize** on the same 10 mu. Here I switch to no-tillage; there is no time to waste between harvests, and the maize roots exploit the wheat root channels. I plant a hybrid variety such as Nongda 372 for its high density tolerance and fast grain filling. Fertilizer is 15 kg N, 5 kg P₂O₅ and 3 kg K₂O per mu, banded at sowing and side-dressed at the large trumpet stage. Maize needs less irrigation than wheat here; two well-timed irrigations at silking and grain filling are usually enough. I plan three pesticide applications—herbicide at the 3–5 leaf stage, plus insecticide and fungicide as needed. A good summer should give me about 620 kg/mu.

Rotary tillage suits wheat establishment on stubble-heavy fields, while no-tillage saves critical days between wheat harvest and maize sowing.
